audited_items.title: Add explicit overflow behavior.
source_evidence: compiler/anvil.py: numeric expression generation wraps arithmetic results, operands, and all numeric built-in results in anvil_check_number; division checks finite operands/results.
runtime/anvil_runtime.c: anvil_check_number rejects non-finite doubles with source path/line and exit code 2.
tests: tests/test_compiler.py::CompilerTests::test_non_finite_numeric_results_report_source_location: passed for arithmetic overflow, comparison intermediate, and sqrt(-1)
tests/test_compiler.py::CompilerTests::test_accumulation_and_for_step_overflow_report_source_location: passed for local add, local subtract, and for-loop step overflow
tests/test_compiler.py::CompilerTests::test_udp_nan_receive_reports_source_location: passed end-to-end by sending an IEEE NaN UDP payload and checking source path/line and exit code 2
tests/test_compiler.py::CompilerTests::test_udp_finite_receive_and_missing_socket_remain_supported: passed finite 42.5 payload and unavailable-socket zero behavior
audited_items.missing_or_limitations: Item #47 behavior passed independent review on 15439b5. Overall QA scored 90/100, below the required 98/100 bar, so broader evaluation work continues and another overall review is pending. This detects non-finite results but does not prevent every finite precision loss or integer-style wraparound because Anvil uses double values.
acceptance_criteria: Define overflow/non-finite runtime behavior.
Report the Anvil source path and line and exit deterministically.
Cover direct overflow, non-finite intermediates used in comparisons, and invalid math results.
Document the behavior and get independent review.
audited_items.verification_result: COMPLETE: the 61-test suite, extension validation, Python/JSON/diff checks, MSVC numeric demo, and independent review of 15439b5 pass for item #47. The review scored 90/100 overall and found no code defect. Issues #30 and #31 are resolved and closed; broader QA remains below 98/100.

source_evidence: compiler/anvil.py: LANGUAGE_VERSION is 1; parse() accepts one optional leading 'language version 1' directive and rejects malformed, duplicate, late, or unsupported versions with source-located diagnostics.
tests: tests/test_compiler.py::CompilerTests::test_language_version_header_and_legacy_default: passed for explicit version 1 and unversioned compatibility

audited_items.missing_or_limitations: Only language version 1 is currently implemented. The directive establishes compatibility boundaries for future syntax changes; it does not add alternate dialect behavior or project-manifest version selection.
acceptance_criteria: Allow an optional language version declaration before source code.
Preserve legacy unversioned files as the current version.
Reject malformed, duplicate, late, and unsupported version declarations with path-and-line diagnostics.
Document the current version and compatibility policy and obtain independent review.
